`src/markdown-inline.js` is a finished renderer that turns one paragraph of inline Markdown into HTML, and its test suite is failing. Find and fix the faults in the module. Keep every behaviour the passing tests already pin down, keep the exported names `renderInline` and `escapeHtml`, and do not weaken the module by special-casing the inputs the tests happen to use.

The renderer walks the text once, and at each position tries a backslash escape, a code span, an autolink, an inline link and an emphasis run, in that order; anything else is ordinary text with `&`, `<`, `>` and `"` escaped as entities. A backslash before ASCII punctuation writes that character literally and is otherwise itself. A code span opens on a run of backticks and closes on the next run of exactly the same length, with the text between them taken verbatim; if the content both starts and ends with a space and is not all spaces, one space is dropped from each end, and an opening run that never closes is literal text.

An autolink is `<` followed by an absolute URI, meaning a scheme of letters, digits, `+`, `.` or `-` then a colon and no whitespace or angle brackets, or by an email address whose local part may hold letters, digits and the usual mail punctuation such as `.`, `+`, `-`, `_`, `'` and `%`; it becomes a link whose text is the address itself and whose destination is that URI or the address with a `mailto:` prefix. An inline link is `[text](destination)` with an optional `"title"` or `'title'`, where the brackets may nest, the destination may be wrapped in angle brackets or run to the closing parenthesis with balanced parentheses inside, and both may carry backslash escapes; the text is rendered as inline Markdown except that it may not contain another link. A destination is written into the `href` with its existing percent-triplets left exactly as they are, with space, `"`, `<`, `>`, backslash and backtick percent-encoded, and with the attribute then escaped for HTML.

Emphasis pairs runs of `*` or `_`. A run may open when the character after it is neither absent nor whitespace, and may close when the character before it is neither absent nor whitespace. An underscore run additionally may not open directly after a letter or digit, and may not close directly before one, so `foo_bar_baz` is plain text while `foo*bar*baz` is not. An opening run of two or more delimiters first looks for a closing run of at least two, which produces `<strong>`, and falls back to a closing run of one, which produces `<em>`; the delimiters used are taken from the start of the opening run and the end of the closing run, and whatever is left over belongs to the enclosed text, which is rendered recursively. The search for a closing run skips backslash-escaped characters and does not otherwise look inside other constructs. A non-string argument throws `TypeError`. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list

tools.name: job_output

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

All 12 tests pass now. Summary of the faults found and fixed in `src/markdown-inline.js`:

1. **Double percent-encoding of existing triplets** — `encodeDestination` prepended `%25` to already-valid percent-triplets (turning `%20` into `%2520`) instead of leaving them exactly as-is. Fixed to reuse the literal `%` unchanged.

2. **Email autolink regex missing `+`** — `AUTOLINK_EMAIL`'s local-part character class omitted `+`, so addresses like `a+b@example.com` failed to match and fell through to plain escaped text. Added `+` to the class.

3. **Emphasis open/close checks inverted between markers** — `canOpen`/`canClose` applied the "not adjacent to alphanumeric" restriction to `*` instead of `_`, backwards from the spec (only underscore runs have that extra restriction). Swapped the marker check from `'*'` to `'_'` in both functions.

4. **Code span closing-run length not required to match** — `codeSpan` accepted any closing run of length ≥ 1 instead of requiring it to equal the opening run's length, so `` ``a`b`` `` closed too early on the single backtick. Fixed to require `closing === length`.

5. **Code span space-trimming used `.trim()` instead of dropping exactly one space per side** — this stripped multiple/interior whitespace incorrectly (e.g. `` `  a  ` `` should keep one space each side). Fixed to slice off exactly one leading and one trailing space when content starts and ends with a space and isn't all spaces.

The fixes were minimal, targeted, and didn't special-case any specific test input — each corrected a general rule (percent-triplet preservation, email local-part charset, marker-specific emphasis rules, exact-length code-fence matching, single-space trimming) as described in the spec.

goal.objective:
`src/markdown-inline.js` is a finished renderer that turns one paragraph of inline Markdown into HTML, and its test suite is failing. Find and fix the faults in the module. Keep every behaviour the passing tests already pin down, keep the exported names `renderInline` and `escapeHtml`, and do not weaken the module by special-casing the inputs the tests happen to use.

The renderer walks the text once, and at each position tries a backslash escape, a code span, an autolink, an inline link and an emphasis run, in that order; anything else is ordinary text with `&`, `<`, `>` and `"` escaped as entities. A backslash before ASCII punctuation writes that character literally and is otherwise itself. A code span opens on a run of backticks and closes on the next run of exactly the same length, with the text between them taken verbatim; if the content both starts and ends with a space and is not all spaces, one space is dropped from each end, and an opening run that never closes is literal text.

An autolink is `<` followed by an absolute URI, meaning a scheme of letters, digits, `+`, `.` or `-` then a colon and no whitespace or angle brackets, or by an email address whose local part may hold letters, digits and the usual mail punctuation such as `.`, `+`, `-`, `_`, `'` and `%`; it becomes a link whose text is the address itself and whose destination is that URI or the address with a `mailto:` prefix. An inline link is `[text](destination)` with an optional `"title"` or `'title'`, where the brackets may nest, the destination may be wrapped in angle brackets or run to the closing parenthesis with balanced parentheses inside, and both may carry backslash escapes; the text is rendered as inline Markdown except that it may not contain another link. A destination is written into the `href` with its existing percent-triplets left exactly as they are, with space, `"`, `<`, `>`, backslash and backtick percent-encoded, and with the attribute then escaped for HTML.

Emphasis pairs runs of `*` or `_`. A run may open when the character after it is neither absent nor whitespace, and may close when the character before it is neither absent nor whitespace. An underscore run additionally may not open directly after a letter or digit, and may not close directly before one, so `foo_bar_baz` is plain text while `foo*bar*baz` is not. An opening run of two or more delimiters first looks for a closing run of at least two, which produces `<strong>`, and falls back to a closing run of one, which produces `<em>`; the delimiters used are taken from the start of the opening run and the end of the closing run, and whatever is left over belongs to the enclosed text, which is rendered recursively. The search for a closing run skips backslash-escaped characters and does not otherwise look inside other constructs. A non-string argument throws `TypeError`. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.
